raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

A multi-layer EAGLE draft replays one CUDA graph per draft step. When the draft is fused into the unified pool (`--enable-unified-memory`), its FlashAttention backend translates KV ids and so could neither record its draft-extend metadata in the graph nor stage it: every step's replay rebuilt the metadata eagerly first. The steps of a chain extend the same window, so all of those rebuilds produced the same tables: lengths, prefix sums, the translated full and sliding-window page tables, and the sliding-window write ids. In a traced Inkling-Small MTP run on fa4 (TP 8, SM90), the unified pool's draft-extend host time per cycle was twice the default pool's.

## Modifications

- A translating FlashAttention backend now stages the draft-extend metadata once per cycle from the cycle's plan (`layers/attention/flashattention_backend.py`). One launch fills the lengths and prefix sums; the page tables come from the plan's read table, which the first step backend builds in place and the others copy; the sliding-window write ids come from the plan, as before. A backend whose reads stay virtual has no plan table to stage from, so it reports no staging support.
- The multi-layer runner stages through an explicit `stage_draft_extend_metadata` entry (`layers/attention/base_attn_backend.py`), which Inkling's short-conv wrapper now exposes too (`layers/attention/linear/inkling_sconv_backend.py`).
- With staging available, these drafts can take the single combined draft graph, as on the default pool (unless `SGLANG_ENABLE_SINGLE_CG_DRAFT=0`).
- On a translating pool the chain stages after verify, not before it (`speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py`). Staging before verify would move the scheduler's write-after-read fence to the target's read end, but this pool still translates after verify: Inkling's draft graph maps its checkpoint slots through the live table, and a widened window binds its own plan. A request freed once that fence passes would unmap a slot the draft is about to write.

Tests:
- CUDA (SM90), `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_flashattention_graph_metadata.py`: staging fills exactly the tables the per-step rebuild did, at page sizes 1 and 128, with and without a sliding-window pool; one plan serves every step backend with one build per table; a captured step reads each cycle's staging in place, including after pages move. The staging capability for static, translating, DCP and topk > 1 backends.
- CPU, `test/registered/unit/spec/test_draft_extend_metadata_staging.py`: staging backends get one staging call per cycle and no per-step rebuild; others keep the rebuild; the wrapper stages its attention tables, then its slot indices. A unified chain is not staged before verify and keeps the draft's fence, while a static pool's chain is staged early and its replay reads checkpoint slots as staged.

## Accuracy Tests

SM90, `thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small`, TP 8, `--attention-backend fa4`, `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-draft-model-path thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small --enable-multi-layer-eagle --speculative-num-steps 8 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 9 --speculative-use-rejection-sampling`, radix cache, overlap scheduler, on main `669292bacc` with this PR and the other open unified-memory PRs applied. sgl-eval GSM8K, all 1314 test questions, `--temperature 0 --max-tokens 2048`. Default pool against `--enable-unified-memory`; median accept length from the scheduler logs. The unified-memory servers ran with `SGLANG_DEBUG_POISON_POOL=1`, so a read of a never-written pool row shows up as a wrong answer.

| CUDA graphs | GSM8K (default / unified) | one pool only right (default / unified), p | accept length (default / unified) |
|---|---|---|---|
| off | 0.9543 / 0.9482 | 12 / 4, p = 0.08 | 3.88 / 3.88 |
| on | 0.9543 / 0.9543 | 9 / 9, p = 1.00 | 3.88 / 3.92 |

Neither row's difference is significant at 0.05, which does not by itself establish equivalence. An earlier run on main `259f0131c9` gave 0.9543 / 0.9521 with graphs off and 0.9551 / 0.9513 with graphs on, also not significant. The unified pool's score is equal or slightly lower in all four runs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same setup on main `259f0131c9`, CUDA graphs on, with #46376 in both builds so both pools run 14 requests at once. `--enable-unified-memory` against the default pool on the same build, before and after this PR; a second default-pool server gives the run-to-run spread in parentheses.

| load | req/s gap, before / after | mean TTFT gap, before / after | mean ITL gap, before / after | decode step gap at equal batch size, before / after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24 requests of 512 input / 2048 output tokens, one at a time | -12.6% / -1.3% (1.8) | +2.8% / +1.4% (0.4) | +14.9% / +1.3% (1.9) | +12.6% / +1.4% |
| 100 requests of 512 input / 4096 output tokens, concurrency 128 | -7.9% / -1.0% (1.6) | +7.3% / +1.1% (2.0) | +7.9% / +0.9% (1.3) | +8.2% / +0.7% |
| 192 requests sharing a 4096-token prefix + 128 tokens, 2048 output tokens, concurrency 192 | -7.8% / -1.2% (2.0) | +8.2% / +0.8% (3.5) | +11.3% / +1.3% (2.7) | +10.9% / +2.3% |

Before this PR the unified server logs that it cannot refresh its metadata for a combined graph and falls back to per-step draft graphs; after it, it captures the combined graph. That combined graph already samples the rejection-sampling proposal in the graph, so #46385's gain on unified fa4 does not add to this one: with both applied, unified fa4 runs this path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+class TestDraftExtendStagingCapability(CustomTestCase):
+    """Which backends stage their draft-extend tables once per draft cycle: a
+    static backend whose graph records the tables keeps doing so, a
+    translating one stages them from the cycle's plan, and one whose reads
+    stay virtual reports no staging, having no plan table to stage from."""
+
+    def _backend(self, *, topk=1, translating, reads_translated=True, in_graph=True):
+        b = FlashAttentionBackend.__new__(FlashAttentionBackend)
+        b.topk = topk
+        b.runner_ids = SimpleNamespace(
+            is_translating=translating, reads_are_translated=reads_translated
+        )
+        b.draft_extend_metadata_captured_in_graph = lambda: in_graph
+        return b
+
+    def test_staging_capability(self):
+        cases = (
+            (dict(translating=False), True),
+            (dict(translating=False, in_graph=False), False),
+            (dict(translating=True, in_graph=False), True),
+            (dict(translating=True, in_graph=False, reads_translated=False), False),
+            (dict(translating=True, in_graph=False, topk=2), False),
+            (dict(translating=False, topk=2), False),
+        )
+        for kwargs, stages in cases:
+            with self.subTest(**kwargs):
+                backend = self._backend(**kwargs)
+                self.assertEqual(backend.supports_draft_extend_metadata_staging, stages)
+
+
+def _page_runner_ids(req_to_token, page_size, full_v2p, swa_v2p):
+    """A unified `RunnerIds` over page tables: a virtual token id maps to its
+    page's physical page, and an unbound page (-1) to the sink."""
+
+    def through(v2p):
+        def write(ids):
+            pages = v2p[ids // page_size].clamp(min=0).to(ids.dtype)
+            return pages * page_size + ids % page_size
+
+        return write
+
+    runner_ids = RunnerIds.__new__(RunnerIds)
+    runner_ids.req_to_token = req_to_token
+    runner_ids.page_size = page_size
+    runner_ids.device = req_to_token.device
+    runner_ids.is_translating = True
+    runner_ids.defer_read_translate = False
+    runner_ids._rows = torch.arange(req_to_token.shape[0], device=req_to_token.device)

+    step's replay. The staged tables must be exactly what the per-step
+    rebuild produced: lengths, prefix sums, physical page tables and the

+    BS, RAW_BS, WIDTH, PAGES = 4, 3, 3, 6

+    def _setup(self, ps, use_swa):
+        device = "cuda"

+        req_to_token = torch.zeros((rows, pages * ps), dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+        for row in range(1, rows):
+            req_to_token[row] = torch.arange(
+                row * pages * ps, (row + 1) * pages * ps, device=device
+            )
+        num_virtual_pages = rows * pages
+        full = torch.arange(num_virtual_pages, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+        full = full.flip(0).contiguous()
+        full[0] = 0
+        swa = None
+        if use_swa:
+            swa = torch.arange(num_virtual_pages, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+            swa[pages + 1] = -1  # an unbound sliding-window page reads the sink
+        runner_ids = _page_runner_ids(req_to_token, ps, full, swa)
+        # Request 0 is the padded lane's sink row.
+        req_pool_indices = torch.tensor([2, 4, 1, 0], device=device)
+        # Every live lane holds its whole window; lane 3 is the padded one.
+        seq_lens = torch.tensor([ps + 3, 2 * ps + 3, 4, 1], device=device)
+        extend = torch.full((self.BS,), self.WIDTH, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        window = torch.cat(
+            [
+                req_to_token[int(r), int(n) - self.WIDTH : int(n)]
+                for r, n in zip(
+                    req_pool_indices[: self.RAW_BS], seq_lens[: self.RAW_BS]
+                )
+            ]
+        )

+
+    def _plan(self, runner_ids, req_pool_indices, seq_lens, window):
+        return IterationIds(
+            source=runner_ids,
+            req_pool_indices=req_pool_indices[: self.RAW_BS],
+            seq_lens=seq_lens[: self.RAW_BS],

+            "cache_seqlens": torch.full(
+                (self.BS,), -9, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+            ),
+            # The prefix sums' leading zero is never rewritten, as allocated.
+            "cu_seqlens_q": torch.zeros(self.BS + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),

+        )
+        draft_worker = SimpleNamespace(
+            cuda_graph_runner_for_draft_extend=SimpleNamespace(
+                require_mlp_tp_gather=False,
+                max_bs=BS,
+                disable_padding=False,
+                stage_shared_reads=lambda **kwargs: staged_calls.append(kwargs),
+            ),
+            draft_extend_attn_backend_list=[backend],
+            target_worker=SimpleNamespace(model_runner=target_runner),
+            draft_runner_list=[SimpleNamespace(runner_ids=runner_ids)],
+            topk=1,
+            speculative_num_draft_tokens=WIDTH,
+            _compute_boundary_kv_locs_positions=lambda batch: (
+                torch.arange(RAW_BS * WIDTH),
+                None,
+            ),
+        )
+        batch = SimpleNamespace(
+            forward_mode=ForwardMode.DECODE,
+            seq_lens=torch.tensor([9, 8, 7]),
+            req_pool_indices=torch.tensor([3, 1, 2]),
+        )
+        staged = MultiLayerEagleDraftWorker._draft_extend_plan_for_decode(
+            draft_worker, batch
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(len(staged_calls), int(staged))
+        draft_runner = object()
+        worker = SimpleNamespace(
+            draft_worker=SimpleNamespace(last_draft_extend_staged=staged),
+            target_worker=draft_worker.target_worker,
+            _draft_worker=SimpleNamespace(draft_runner=draft_runner),
+        )
+        fence = MultiLayerEagleWorkerV2.last_shared_read_runner.fget(worker)
+        return staged, fence is target_runner, fence is draft_runner
+
+    def _replay_track_slots(self, backend, virtual_slots):
+        batch = SimpleNamespace(
+            forward_mode=ForwardMode.DRAFT_EXTEND_V2, mamba_track_indices=virtual_slots
+        )
+        backend.init_forward_metadata_in_graph(batch)
+        return backend.short_conv_backend.sconv_metadata.track_cache_indices
+
+    def test_a_unified_chain_keeps_the_draft_fence(self):
+        bundle, allocator = build_tri_pool(lazy=False)
+        table = bundle.req_to_token_pool
+        runner_ids = RunnerIds(
+            req_to_token=table.req_to_token,
+            token_to_kv_pool_allocator=allocator,
+            token_to_kv_pool=bundle.token_to_kv_pool,
+            page_size=1,
+            device="cpu",
+        )
+        backend = self._inkling(runner_ids, table.state_sub_pool)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._stage_and_fence(backend, runner_ids), (False, False, True)
+        )
+        # Freeing the first slot moves the last one into its place.
+        slots = allocator.state_slots.alloc(4)
+        allocator.state_slots.free(slots[:1])
+        checkpoint = slots[-1:]
+        physical = allocator.mamba_allocator.ids.virtual_to_physical[checkpoint]
+        self.assertNotEqual(physical.tolist(), checkpoint.tolist())
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._replay_track_slots(backend, checkpoint).tolist(), physical.tolist()
+        )
+        # What the draft's fence covers: a free after the target's read end would
+        # unmap the slot this replay is about to read.
+        allocator.state_slots.free(checkpoint)
+        self.assertEqual(self._replay_track_slots(backend, checkpoint).tolist(), [-1])
+
+    def test_a_static_chain_stages_before_verify(self):
+        # A static pool's request table holds the state pool's own slot ids.
+        runner_ids = RunnerIds(
+            req_to_token=torch.zeros((BS, 16), dtype=torch.int32),
+            token_to_kv_pool_allocator=SimpleNamespace(
+                hands_out_virtual_ids=False, state_id_spaces=dict
+            ),
+            token_to_kv_pool=SimpleNamespace(
+                id_spaces=lambda: {
+                    IdSpaceKind.FULL: IdSpace(key=(IdSpaceKind.FULL, None))
+                }
+            ),
+            page_size=1,
+            device="cpu",
+        )
+        backend = self._inkling(runner_ids, "mamba")
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self._stage_and_fence(backend, runner_ids), (True, True, False)
+        )
+        checkpoint = torch.tensor([2])
+        self.assertIs(self._replay_track_slots(backend, checkpoint), checkpoint)
+
+
+class TestBaseStaging(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_a_backend_without_staging_refuses_to_stage(self):
+        backend = AttentionBackend.__new__(AttentionBackend)
+        self.assertFalse(backend.supports_draft_extend_metadata_staging)
+        with self.assertRaises(NotImplementedError):
+            backend.stage_draft_extend_metadata(SimpleNamespace())
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
